messages:
jess: Hey — running into a weird combo of issues with redwoodctl local-test on my M2 Mac. Trying to mount a local dir into the test runtime but the path appears empty inside the container, and on top of that redwoodctl is dropping into an interactive auth flow which hangs our CI.

jess: Command I ran: `redwoodctl local-test --mount ./sample-data:/app/data --profile=workspaces --debug` (redwoodctl v0.28.1, macOS 13.5, zsh + oh-my-zsh).

samir: Can you paste the minimal debug output? Also does this reproduce with docker or only podman/podman-desktop?

jess: minimal snippet from --debug:
```
INFO  local-test: starting runtime
WARN  mount: requested mount ./sample-data -> /app/data: resolved to /Users/jess/code/myproj/sample-data
ERROR runtime: mount target /app/data not present after startup
INFO  auth: token expired, starting device code flow (opening browser)
```
In CI the device flow causes the job to wait forever. Locally it opens browser (annoying).

olivia: two separate problems IMO: 1) mount not showing up, 2) auth fallback to device-code in noninteractive env. For mounts: are you using podman rootless or plain Docker? Podman on Apple silicon has path-mapping quirks when HOME is a symlink.

jess: i'm on Docker Desktop (default). But i do keep my dotfiles and home under a symlinked path (/Users/jess -> /mnt/data/jess), could that be it?

samir: yes — we've had a case where the local runtime canonicalizes the host path, then the VM/Docker path translation doesn't match the container bind target. Try `realpath ./sample-data` and mount that. Also check XDG_CONFIG_HOME / REDWOOD_LOCAL_MOUNTS env.

jess: tried `realpath`, still empty. Also noticed REDWOOD_LOCAL_MOUNTS env isn't set in my shell.

olivia: for the auth issue: redwoodctl will attempt a silent refresh and if it gets a 401 it falls back to interactive device flow. In CI you should pre-populate REDWOOD_TOKEN or use a service account flow to avoid interactive fallback. We should probably detect CI/noninteractive and error instead of launching device flow.

devx-bot: Known issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/3827 — local-test mounts + symlinked HOME on macOS can result in empty mounts (triaged, workaround documented).

samir: Workarounds to try: 1) ensure host path is inside /Users (or Docker shared path), 2) pass absolute path from `docker inspect` host path, 3) run `redwoodctl local-test --no-auth-proxy` or set `REDWOOD_AUTH_NONINTERACTIVE=1` in CI to avoid device flow.

jess: CI workaround that worked for me: pre-auth with a token file in the job and export REDWOOD_TOKEN. Example:
```
# CI job steps
- run: redwoodctl auth login --service-account-key "$SA_KEY" --output token > /tmp/rw_token
- run: export REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/rw_token)
- run: redwoodctl local-test --mount $(pwd)/sample-data:/app/data --debug
```
That removed the interactive auth prompt and the runtime then failed fast on the mount (so at least CI exits instead of hanging).

olivia: thanks for the snippet — can you open a tiny repro with steps and include `docker inspect` output and your `realpath` results? Put it in a gist and link it here; we'll add a quick note to the local-test docs and add a CI-detection guard to the auth flow.

jess: opened gist: https://gist.github.com/jess/9a7bcd (contains repro and `docker inspect` outputs). Also created issue in infra repo linking the gist.

samir: i'll pick up the CI-detection change. Can you also add a small integration test that runs local-test in a docker-in-docker runner so we can catch mounts+symlink regressions?

jess: yep i'll add a test and a short doc blurb for onboarding. Thanks! :thumbsup:

ci-bot: CI job 78342 re-run scheduled after token pre-auth was added.

olivia: follow-up todo: docs + add noninteractive failure mode to redwoodctl (instead of launching device flow) — filing a follow-up task. :eyes:
